function: above_phy, p. 6: the learned MADRL policy outputs UAV accelerations, i.e., it controls the UAV cluster's trajectory toward a light spot center computed by a non-learned beam-splitting method (pp. 5-8).
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Excluded as above_phy: the learned component is an attention-based MADDPG whose action is the UAV acceleration (p. 6: 'The control of the UAV is mainly achieved by adjusting the velocities in three directions', action a = (ax, ay, az); p. 5: 'The UAV flight is controlled by the neural network output'). The alignment target is computed without learning (p. 5: 'the CUAV predicts the light spot center position based on the position of the AUV, using the sea surface model combined with mathematical methods. Then, the CUAV flies to the predicted position'; beam-splitting and binning, pp. 6-8). The learning therefore controls the trajectory of a UAV cluster (core UAV flying to the spot center, assistance UAVs keeping the Koch-snowflake formation, collision avoidance, pp. 6, 10), which rule 4 lists as above the physical layer. The aerial-link exception does not apply because no transmit power, resource allocation, or beam is learned: the AUV laser is fixed and vertical (p. 3: 'For a vertically aligned AUV laser'). The link is also a single blue-green laser to single photodiode IM/DD optical link with no RIS (p. 3; Table I, p. 9), not an RF MIMO system. Even if alignment were read as a physical-layer task, it is pointing/tracking (close to positioning), which is not one of the seven areas, so the work would fail 'function'.
